title: Audit-traceable reprocess orchestrator with dynamic windowing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our console telemetry pipelines occasionally require reprocessing (schema evolution, late-arriving events, bug fixes in transforms). Current backfill tooling is brittle for long-running tenant-wide reprocesses: it lacks auditable checkpoints, dynamic window sizing to adapt to hot shards, and an operator-friendly orchestration surface. This ticket implements an audit-traceable reprocess orchestrator that: 1) segments work into dynamic time/size windows, 2) persists immutable audit traces and resume tokens per-tenant, and 3) provides conditional transforms to handle schema evolution without blocking the whole job.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Operator can start/stop/inspect reprocess jobs with per-tenant visibility and immutable audit trail (who started, why, checksums).
- Reprocess is resumable after failures using resume tokens; re-running the same job is idempotent (no duplicated telemetry).
- Dynamic windowing adjusts segment size based on observed processing latency and output throughput to stay within SLOs while maximizing throughput.
- Conditional transform hooks allow applying migration logic only when an event matches a predicate (avoid global schema migration failures).
- Metrics and dashboards show per-window success/failure rates and estimated completion time.

High-level approach:
- Controller service (stateless) manages job lifecycle and publishes immutable audit records to a job-audit topic (Kafka).
- Worker pool reads window assignments from an assignment topic and writes per-window checkpoints to durable store (Dynamo/Spanner); each checkpoint includes a stable resume token (monotonic offset + shard fingerprint + schema-version).
- Dynamic windowing controller samples recent worker latencies and adjusts future window durations for hot shards; cold shards get larger windows to reduce overhead.
- Conditional transforms implemented as a small WASM sandbox per-worker so operators can deploy migration logic without a full rollout.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Complexity: introducing WASM sandboxes and immutable audit topics increases system complexity and operational surface. Chosen because it prevents human error during schema migrations and enables safe per-tenant fixes.
- Storage: durable per-window checkpoints add storage cost but are necessary for auditable resumes and troubleshooting. We'll compress and TTL older checkpoints after job completion to limit costs.
- Latency vs throughput: dynamic windowing may temporarily oscillate; controller will use dampening heuristics to avoid thrashing.

Acceptance tests:
- Start a tenant reprocess, kill half the workers mid-run, restart, verify completion and no duplicate outputs.
- Deploy a transform that only upgrades events with field X present; verify other events pass through unchanged.
- Simulate schema change that would previously blow up the pipeline; confirm job continues with per-window failures surfaced.

Success metrics:
- Mean time to resume after worker/process failure < 90s.
- No duplicated telemetry artifacts in reprocessed indices for test tenants.
- Operator time to identify cause for failed window < 15 minutes via dashboards and audit traces.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: WASM sandbox could slow hot-path processing. Mitigation: keep sandbox warm, precompile common transforms, and limit transform CPU budgets.
- Risk: large numbers of tiny checkpoints increase load on datastore. Mitigation: enforce minimum window size and aggregate low-volume checkpoints for cold shards.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (spec + ops review, 1 week): design doc, security review, cost estimate, and operator CLI spec.
- M2 (controller + audit topic, 2 weeks): implement job lifecycle, immutable audit publishing, basic UI endpoints.
- M3 (workers + resume tokens, 3 weeks): worker assignment consumer and durable checkpointing with resume logic.
- M4 (dynamic windowing + heuristics, 2 weeks): adaptive window controller and metrics.
- M5 (WASM conditional transforms + tests, 2 weeks): integrate sandbox and run migration scenarios.
- M6 (staging validation + dashboards, 1 week): run replay on staging tenants, create dashboards, and harden SLOs.

Rollout plan:
1. Internal alpha with infra and SRE teams on low-volume tenants.
2. Gradual opt-in for customers with small quota, monitor.
3. Full rollout once metrics stable and runbook validated.

comments: 2025-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after SRE postmortem for incident 2025-02-27. Need explicit auditability; current ad-hoc reprocess caused duplicate rows in customer indices.
2025-03-12 - Maya Chen: Design review notes: prefer immutable audit topic instead of updating job rows in place. Concerned about Kafka retention cost — recommend TTL + compaction on audit topic.

2025-03-14 - Liam O'Connor: POC of resume token format posted in PR #118. Using <shard>-<offset>-<schemaHash> to guarantee monotonicity and detect schema drift. Seeking feedback from storage team on checkpoint throughput.

2025-03-16 - Diego Ruiz (SRE): Ran load tests on the controller: 2000 concurrent windows produced controller CPU spike. Action: introduce backpressure and rate-limit window assignment to 250/s. Filed follow-up ENG-91800 for controller autoscaling behavior.
2025-03-18 - Priya Raman (Product): Confirmed operator UX requirements and asked for 'dry-run' mode that computes estimated runtime and cost. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-19 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented basic dynamic windowing with exponential smoothing; initial staging run shows 24% improvement in throughput for hot shards. Observed a 6% CPU overhead from WASM transforms in warm cache. We'll precompile heavy transforms as a next step.

2025-03-20 - QA (Maya Chen): Integration tests passing in staging for tenant 'alpha-demo'. One failing case: events with legacy timestamp format cause transform exception; created bug ENG-91412 to add robust timestamp parsing in worker transform harness.
